notes: Bash(uv:*) permission now active in user settings; iteration 2 ran real Python end-to-end. All four with-skill runs and three of four baselines actually executed code against the data.

Eval 1 (catalog): both runs computed identical real coefficients. Skill version applied the new Step 5 closing subsection — explicitly kept Age in and explained OVB risk; baseline did not warn. Skill differentiation is on tooling (pyrsm/polars), sidecar usage, and the new pushback language.

Eval 2 (diamonds): both runs successfully diagnosed the linear-spec residual pathology and refit as log-log with elasticity ~1.81. Skill version produced the per-clarity-level exact 100*(exp(beta)-1)% table and noted the scatter-vs-regression direction issue; baseline did neither.
Eval 3 (path refusal): unchanged from iteration 1 — clean refusal vs. baseline ls + generic plan. Most decisive single eval.

Eval 4 (OVB pushback) is the iteration 2 highlight. Both versions push back on the reasoning, but they reach DIFFERENT recommendations: skill recommends keeping Age in (consistent with the user's pedagogy), baseline recommends the reduced model with the full model in a footnote. Skill also explicitly names the trigger thresholds, presents all four remediation options, and excludes the Intercept from the trigger check (a thoughtful detail). Baseline does the OVB math correctly but lacks the structured protocol and lands on the opposite recommendation.

Cost of the skill: ~+27s wall-clock and ~+16K tokens per eval on average vs. baseline. Mostly attributable to reading SKILL.md plus references/regress.md and producing the structured pedagogical writeup. Reasonable for a class-facing tool.

Compared to iteration 1: with-skill pass rate stayed at 1.00; baseline pass rate moved from 0.20 to 0.40 because (a) Bash now works so the catalog baseline produces output, and (b) the new eval 4 has a baseline that does substantial work. Delta narrowed from +0.80 to +0.60 — still the dominant effect, and now backed by genuine end-to-end execution rather than artifact-by-other-means.
